The *Sattuppalamālikātherīapadāna* (Thi Ap 8) is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therīapadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past-life meritorious deeds and spiritual attainments of a Buddhist nun (*therī*). SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals extensive text reuse with other Pali literature, identifying 118 matching passages across 36 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most significant textual parallel is found in the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which contains substantial verbatim overlap spanning segments §0.3–16.4 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring stock verses—most noticeably across segments §16–22—are shared with multiple other biographical poems in the *Therīapadāna*, including the *Ekapiṇḍapātadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 6), *Naḷamālikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 5 and Thi-Ap 16), *Ekūposathikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 11), and *Pañcadīpadāyikātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 15), reflecting standard formulaic expressions of spiritual realization and stock biographical framing [DharmaNexus]. Across language corpora, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring algorithmic matches with Tibetan narrative texts, such as the *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144) and the *Jātakamālā* (D4150), though these represent machine alignments rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
